question: Is alarm persistence a better precision/recall trade than simply raising the alarm threshold on the same frozen predictions?

deployable_candidates.rule: Alarm when probability >= m times the unchanged frozen annual threshold, capped at 1. No labels or evaluation outcomes are used to set m.
deployable_candidates.acceptance: Same per-year primary conditions as alarm-persistence-v1 versus the unchanged control: episode precision higher, FP windows lower, alarmed positive runs not below, window recall drop at most 0.02. Pass requires all six positive years for the same multiplier.
deployable_candidates.inference: Paired full-HARP bootstrap (1000 draws, seed 24) of episode precision and FP-window differences versus control.

oracle_references.nature: Diagnostic only. Thresholds are chosen using evaluation labels, so they are not deployable, have no uncertainty interval and cannot be adopted.
oracle_references.threshold_grid: Distinct arm probabilities of the year's evaluation windows; alarm when probability >= t.
oracle_references.matched_recall: For each persistence candidate (k=3, k=6) and year/arm: the largest t whose window recall is at least the persistence recall. Report achieved recall; ties favour the threshold.
oracle_references.tolerance_reference: Largest t whose window recall is at least control recall minus 0.02. Shows the false-alarm headroom inside the frozen recall tolerance.

verdict_rules.persistence_adds_value: In all six positive years persistence has fewer FP windows and fewer episodes than the matched-recall threshold, for the same k.
verdict_rules.threshold_at_least_as_good: In all six positive years the matched-recall threshold has FP windows less than or equal to persistence, for the same k.
verdict_rules.otherwise: mixed; report per-year wins and losses without a single verdict.
verdict_rules.no_automatic_change: No verdict changes alerts, thresholds or models.

zero_positive_2018: Report FP windows and episodes for deployable candidates only; recall-based references and gates are undefined.
disclosure: Multipliers 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 were chosen after the persistence results were seen, to span a range of false-alarm reductions comparable to or larger than persistence. Not tuned on any threshold result; none had been computed when this file was frozen.
scope: Adaptive development on already inspected years, not an independent test. Counts are overlapping forecast windows and window groupings, not physical flares.
prohibitions: No other multipliers, k values, cooldowns or combined rules after seeing results
No use of future windows in any rule
